p.src: Amongst the gentlemen some had an immense privilege. "They have le pour" says the Journal Historique for the year 1694, page 6; "which means that the courier who marks the billets puts 'pour' before their names—as, 'Pour M. le Prince de Soubise;' instead of which, when he marks the lodging of one who is not royal, he does not put pour, but simply the name—as, 'Le Duc de Gesvres, le Duc de Mazarin.'" p.src: Avoir le tour in England was less glorious but more real. It was a sign of intimate communication with the sovereign. Whoever might be, by birth or favour, in a position to receive direct communications from majesty, had in the wall of their bedchamber a shaft in which was adjusted a bell. The bell sounded, the shaft opened, a royal missive appeared on a gold plate or on a cushion of velvet, and the shaft closed. This was intimate and solemn, the mysterious in the familiar. The shaft was used for no other purpose. The sound of the bell announced a royal message. No one saw who brought it. It was of course merely the page of the king or the queen.

p.src: Not being married, Lord David and Lady Josiana could show themselves together in public without exciting ridicule, and they did so frequently. They often went to plays and racecourses in the same carriage, and sat together in the same box. p.src: No one was cold now. They laid sixteen and a quarter to one on Helmsgail.

p.src: Harry Carleton cried out,—

u.src: Harry Carleton cried out,—

p.src: "It is all over with Phelem-ghe-Madone. I will lay my peerage of Bella-aqua, and my title of Lord Bellew, against the Archbishop of Canterbury's old wig, on Helmsgail."

p.src: "Give me your muzzle," said Kilter to Phelem-ghe-Madone. And stuffing the bloody flannel into the bottle, he washed him all over with gin. The mouth reappeared, and he opened one eyelid. His temples seemed fractured.

p.src: "One round more, my friend," said Kilter; and he added, "for the honour of the low town."

u.src: "One round more, my friend," said Kilter; and he added, "for the honour of the low town."

p.src: The Welsh and the Irish understand each other, still Phelem made no sign of having any power of understanding left.

u.src: The Welsh and the Irish understand each other, still Phelem made no sign of having any power of understanding left.

p.src: Phelem arose, supported by Kilter. It was the twenty-fifth round. From the way in which this Cyclops, for he had but one eye, placed himself in position, it was evident that this was the last round, for no one doubted his defeat. He placed his guard below his chin, with the awkwardness of a failing man.

p.src: Helmsgail, with a skin hardly sweating, cried out,—

u.src: Helmsgail, with a skin hardly sweating, cried out,—

p.src: "I'll back myself, a thousand to one."

u.src: "I'll back myself, a thousand to one."

p.src: Helmsgail, raising his arm, struck out; and, what was strange, both fell. A ghastly chuckle was heard. It was Phelem-ghe-Madone's expression of delight. While receiving the terrible blow given him by Helmsgail on the skull, he had given him a foul blow on the navel.

p.src: Helmsgail, lying on his back, rattled in his throat.

p.src: The spectators looked at him as he lay on the ground, and said, "Paid back!" All clapped their hands, even those who had lost. Phelem-ghe-Madone had given foul blow for foul blow, and had only asserted his right.

p.src: They carried Helmsgail off on a hand-barrow. The opinion was that he would not recover.

p.src: Lord Robartes exclaimed, "I win twelve hundred guineas."

p.src: As she left, Josiana took the arm of Lord David, an act which was tolerated amongst people "engaged." She said to him,—

p.src: "It is very fine, but—"

u.src: "It is very fine, but—"

p.src: "But what?"

u.src: "But what?"

p.src: "I thought it would have driven away my spleen. It has not."

p.src: Lord David stopped, looked at Josiana, shut his mouth, and inflated his cheeks, whilst he nodded his head, which signified attention, and said to the duchess,—

p.src: "For spleen there is but one remedy."
